reader_question: How did each senator and representative vote on the November 2025 bill that ended the shutdown?
grade_line: Documented: the Senate’s and the House Clerk’s roll call records
title: The bill that ended the shutdown passed the Senate 60 to 40 on November 10, 2025, with seven Democrats and one independent joining 52 Republicans, and the House 222 to 209 two days later.
measure_line: How each member voted on H.R. 5371, the continuing appropriations act that became Public Law 119-37: the Senate’s vote on passage, November 10, 2025, and the House’s vote to agree to the Senate’s changes, November 12, 2025
notes: The House had 433 members on November 12, 2025, and two of its 435 seats were vacant. Six Democrats voted yes in the House and two Republicans voted no; one member of each party did not vote.
In the Senate, one Republican voted no, and the two independents, whom the record lists apart from both parties, split one yes and one no.
alt: One square for each member of Congress on the bill that ended the November 2025 shutdown. Senate, November 10, 2025, on passage of the bill: passed 60 to 40. Democrats, 45: 7 yes, 38 no. Independents, 2: 1 yes, 1 no. Republicans, 53: 52 yes, 1 no. House, November 12, 2025, on the motion to concur in the Senate amendment: passed 222 to 209. Democrats, 214: 6 yes, 207 no, 1 not voting. Two seats vacant. Republicans, 219: 216 yes, 2 no, 1 not voting.

table.caption: How each party voted on H.R. 5371 in each chamber, Senate vote 618 of November 10, 2025 and House roll call 285 of November 12, 2025, naming each member who voted the other way or did not vote; every member not named voted with most of their party in that chamber, and the CSV file lists all 533 members

columns.label: Voted the other way or did not vote

chart_notes: Each square is one member, in the party ink: solid for yes, an outline for no, shaded for a member who did not vote, and a faint outline for a vacant seat. Each party is named in words with its count; independents are listed as the Senate record lists them, apart from both parties.
phone_note: Where a party’s name and 20 squares a row do not fit side by side, the name sits above its squares.
notes_internal: Maker A, round 3. Data plan row 92 with the sign-off's conditions on party, rule 14.102. Domain D04 from the sidecar (V7 I054).

Data lead ruling (b): every seat in the party-mark ink; yes solid, no in outline at S61's 1.2 px, not voting in the light fill with no edge, vacant seats as ghost outlines named; Democrats first, then independents as the record lists them, folded into no party, then Republicans; within each group yes, no, not voting. Vacant seats sit between, S48's order.

The House's 435 seats are set by law (2 U.S.C. 2a); the Senate's 100 by the Constitution. Vacant seats are seats less members recorded: House 435 less 433, Senate 100 less 100. Which two House seats were vacant is not in the file and the drawing does not say.
